findings.rootCause: CostVector.finiteNonNegative(value) mapped NaN/+Inf/negative components to Double.MAX_VALUE; plus() then absorbed every other term (MAX_VALUE + x == MAX_VALUE) so objectiveScore() and the rows/workRows tiers tied for all plans and the seeks tier decided (10-row plan with 5 seeks lost to a 1e12-row plan with 0 seeks). EstimateVector.filter built QErrorInterval.heuristic(passRatio, 4.0) treating the pass RATIO as a row count, so interval.upperRows() = 0.5*4 = 2.0 and upper = upperRows * max(pass, 2.0) doubled the input upper bound (400 -> 800); a learned interval around 0.9 gave 1440. In the packed planner ties among astronomically large (overflowed) costs were resolved by relation/state ids assigned in query-text order (finding 3.8.2).
findings.change: CostVector: unknown components (NaN/Inf/negative) map to the named finite ceiling UNKNOWN_COMPONENT_ROWS = 1e15 instead of Double.MAX_VALUE, so costs stay additive (unknown+10 < unknown+1e12, two unknowns > one) and objectiveScore is finite; CostVector.INFINITE is unchanged (it feeds OptimizationGoal cost bounds / goalFingerprint, per the critique). EstimateVector.filter clamps the pass-ratio interval to [0,1] (lowerPass = clamp(min(pass, lower)), upperPass = clamp(max(pass, upper))) and takes upper = min(upperRows, upperRows*upperPass), so a filter can never raise the upper bound and lower <= upper always. DESIGN DEVIATION (deliberate, per critique 3.8.1 major): the packed saturatedAdd/saturatedMultiply/joinRows and PackedIncumbentSearch.objectiveIncrement were NOT re-routed to a 1e150 ceiling. Any ceiling >= ~1e16 loses additivity in doubles exactly like MAX_VALUE does, so a finite COST_CEILING cannot un-tie 1e200-scaled plans (critique point b) and would only move PackedCostNumericContractTest/PackedExecutableFallbackTierTest expectations; MAX_VALUE is finite so PackedWinnerTable's finiteness check never fires on it. Saturated ties are instead resolved deterministically by the canonical content digest (3.8.2), which is what the repro requires. The roadmap 4.4 log-space objective remains the follow-up that removes saturation itself.

findings.rootCause: (a) JoinFactorCostModel.FactorCostEstimate set exactOutputRows = exactOutputRows || bagConfidence >= 1.0, so any bag with confidence 1.0 (a calibration value propagated as a minimum through heuristic operators) was promoted to a DATABASE_EXACT certificate; EvidenceProfile.difference had the same inference (exactMatchCoverage = confidence == 1.0 && right.confidence == 1.0). (b) uncertaintyRows returned 0.0 when any of the five q-error metric keys was merely present (hasQErrorMetric), so plannedCardinalityQError=100 yielded a degenerate [1000,1000] interval while the default q-error 4 yielded [0,3000]. (c) EvidenceProfile.semiJoin returned filter(0.0) for right.rows <= 0 keeping the LEFT confidence (0.9) and ignoring the right side's 0.05 confidence, producing a confident zero from a sketch miss. (d) accessEnablingFactorMask built an int with 1 << ordinal and factorHypergraph tested (mask & 1 << left); the sparse-long kernel has up to 64 factors, so ordinal 33 aliased ordinal 1 and ordinal 63 became bit 31, manufacturing spurious access-enabling bridges.
findings.change: (a) EvidenceProfile gains an explicit `exact` proof bit (new 11-arg canonical constructor; the old 10-arg constructor and of(...) remain as delegating overloads with exact=false). It is set only by EvidenceProfile.exactRows/BagEstimate.exact and survives only row-preserving operations (projection, alias, order, slice, union/cartesian of exact inputs, identity filter, semiJoin with an exact-empty right); heuristic filter, distinct over variables, joins and normalisation drop it. FactorCostEstimate uses alignedBagExact (bag.isExact() && rows aligned) instead of confidence >= 1.0; BagEstimate exposes isExact() and threads the bit through all with* copies, equals/hashCode/toString. EvidenceProfile.difference now requires exact && right.exact for exactMatchCoverage (critique companion item), so an unproven full-coverage MINUS keeps the 0.5 floor instead of a certified zero. (b) removed hasQErrorMetric from the zero branch of uncertaintyRows: only exactness or an explicit uncertainty metric collapses the interval; a reported q-error widens it via rows*(q-1)*(1-confidence). (c) semiJoin with an unproven empty right keeps the zero point estimate but lowers confidence to min(left, right.confidence); an exact-empty right yields an exact empty result. Point estimate deliberately stays 0 (not the critique's 0.5 floor) to avoid flipping packed semi-join strategy choices; LmdbPackedCostModel's call-site floor remains the execution-facing guard. (d) accessEnablingFactorMask returns long (1L << ordinal), factorHypergraph tests 1L << left/right and now throws PackedMemoInvariantException when factors.length > LONG_FACTOR_LIMIT (explicit width invariant per critique); dense callers narrow through denseFactorMask(), which throws if any bit above 31 is set; the mask builder is package-visible and unit-tested up to ordinal 63.

findings.rootCause: Join factor ordinals follow query-text order (collectSelectedFactors/collectStackedFactors), and every exact-cost tie fell back to those ids: DenseJoinStates kept the first continuation reaching a subset (retainDenseCandidate: candidateCost >= best -> skip; bestActiveState: stateId < best; retainParetoState: equal cost vector -> prune the newcomer), DenseCorrelatedStates did the same (publish: costs < only; retainParetoState equal -> prune newcomer; compareDenseCorrelatedGreedyCandidate: Integer.compare(node/state); filter-step and join-step gates: >= / < only), and the budgeted greedy path ranked by relation id (betterGreedyCandidate: relationId < bestRelationId; compareSeedStarts: Integer.compare(factors[]); cheapestFactor: strict < so the first ordinal won). With symmetric finite estimates the two orientations of a binary join tie exactly; with 1e200-scaled estimates every cost saturates at MAX_VALUE and all 24 permutations of a 4-star produced 24 distinct plans (12 shapes); the filtered 4-star gave 6 plans and the budgeted equal-estimate 4-star 24 plans.
findings.change: Roadmap 4.6 'deterministic tie-break on a canonical plan digest', implemented without re-sorting factor arrays (which the critique showed would corrupt collectEmittedPrefixFactors/collectPhysicalPrefixRelations positional semantics). New PackedRelationDigest (package-private visitor) computes a content-only 64-bit digest of a relation's materialized algebra (operator signatures incl. variable names/constants + child order, never packed ids) and composes child digests with the physical implementation tag; a scalar-condition digest (PackedPlanMaterializer.materializeScalar) is used for correlated FILTER steps so the predicate's digest does not include its text-ordered input join. Digests are cached per relation/condition in the enumerator. DenseJoinStates and DenseCorrelatedStates carry a `digests` long column (counted in the byte budget) set at every singleton/append/allocate site; ties are decided by Long.compareUnsigned(digest) with state id as the last resort: DenseJoinStates.displaces() (mutual dominance -> smaller digest survives), bestActiveState, retainDenseCandidate's scalar gate; DenseCorrelatedStates.publish, retainParetoState (equal vectors -> smaller digest), compareDenseCorrelatedGreedyCandidate, the filter-step gate (costDenseCorrelatedFilterStep) and the join-step gate before retainDenseCorrelatedJoinCandidate. Greedy path: betterGreedyCandidate takes digests instead of relation ids, compareSeedStarts and cheapestFactor break row/cost ties by digest. Two guards keep the kernels' work contracts: DenseCorrelatedStates.displaceable() (exploredNodeMasks == 0) lets an equal-cost, canonically smaller continuation displace a retained one only while that one has not been expanded (the greedy seed expands a state as soon as it is created; displacing an expanded state re-costs its transitions in the exhaustive pass and expands two representatives of one continuation), and compareGreedySeedStart orders cost-tied singleton seed starts by fewest legal extensions (a join-graph property) before the digest, so a chain seed still grows from an endpoint with one costed candidate per step. Original-plan preference (tieBreakRank) and requiresWrittenSequence paths are untouched. Verified with the 4-star permutation repro (24 orders, finite and 1e200-scaled), a 4-chain, a filtered 4-star (correlated kernel, finite and saturated), an all-equal-estimate 4-star (exact) and a budgeted (asBudgeted(null, 6)) 4-star with equal and distinct estimates: one plan each.
